title: Keep the Scales Level
idea: An equation is a balance: do the same thing to both sides, undoing the last operation first, until the unknown stands alone, then substitute back to check.
misconceptions: Moves a term to the other side without changing its sign
Multiplies only the first term in a bracket

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Foundations is prior learning (FAL-953), so this runs 4–6 minutes, not 6–8, and some sections are short.

Builds on ex.foundations.pre-substitute, which is also Tess's, so the recall uses her own.watched, own.not-watched, short-version and after lines. The check by substituting back, used in every example, is what ties the two together.

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. Of the question type's methods, inverse operations and collect terms are the lesson, expand-first appears in the slip's correction, and substitute-check is the check in every example. Clearing fractions is left to the question type; it would be a second new step in a 5-minute script.

The two misconceptions not used here (only the fraction terms multiplied by the common denominator; only one term divided when making y the subject) belong to the fractions and make-y-subject unknowns, which this script doesn't teach. Make-y-subject is ex.foundations.pre-change-subject.
Example 3 is a two-part course-style item (SL2.1, a point on a line and an x-intercept), as FAL-953 allows for Foundations.
Live numbers for the turns come from fn-pre-linear-equations (game/engine/situations/linear_equation.gd); the fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

Format 2 (FAL-1043): moved from approved back to draft until it passes the format 2 checks (#188, #190, #191). `node tools/explainer-scripts.mjs --todo` lists what is left: turn lines with numbers or story words, not-yet lines to key to misconceptions, repeated frames and jokes.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Tess again. Out the front of the yard I've got the big scales, for weighing scrap to sell.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: People try all sorts on those scales, a thumb on the pan, a magnet in the boot, and one fella tried to weigh his dog in with his copper.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Today the scales tell us a number nobody wrote down.

board.write: 3 bags + 4 bolts balance 19 bolts. How many in a bag?

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Four. Minus two in brackets, times three, add ten. We'll use that today, to check our answers.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Minus two goes in, in brackets. Three lots of minus two is minus six, and ten more is four. We'll use that today, to check our answers.

not_watched.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_watched.say: Quick one before we start. Tap the answer.

not_watched.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_watched.say: Put the number in where the letter was, in brackets. Then powers, then times, then plus. Three lots of minus two is minus six, and ten more makes four.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Here's the scales. On the left pan, three bags of bolts and four loose ones. On the right, nineteen loose bolts. And it's level.

board.write: Left: 3 bags + 4 bolts.   Right: 19 bolts.   Level.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Every bag holds the same number. Call it x. Then three x plus four equals nineteen. Two sides that balance, with an equals sign between them: that's an equation.

board.write: x = the number of bolts in one bag

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: To solve it, you find the x that keeps it level. And there's one rule. Whatever you do to one pan, you do to the other.

board.write: solve: find the value that makes it true

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So take the four loose bolts off the left. Then take four off the right as well, or the whole thing tips. Three bags balance fifteen.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Then split both pans three ways, and one bag balances five bolts. So x is five.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: See the order? The four went on last, so it comes off first. You undo it backwards, like taking an engine apart.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: My brother took an engine apart once and put it back in the order he liked best. Lovely noise. Didn't go anywhere.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Now on paper. Step one: what we're finding. The value of x that makes four x plus seven equal thirty-one.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step two: undo the last thing first, which is the plus seven. Take seven from both sides. That leaves four x equals twenty-four.

ask.prompt: Why take away 7 before dividing by 4?
choices: +7 was done last, so it comes off first
Dividing first is against the rules

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Yep. Last on, first off. Same as the engine.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Think about how four x plus seven got built: times four, then add seven. You undo it backwards, so the seven comes off first.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step three: divide both sides by four, and x is six.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step four: check it. Six goes back in, in brackets, and four sixes are twenty-four, plus seven is thirty-one. Level.

intro.speaker: tin-can-tess
intro.say: Your go. Last on, first off, and both sides every time.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Sweet as. Both sides, every step.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Choice. And you checked it, too.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Close. Do the same to both sides, not only the one.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Put your answer back in. Does it come out level?

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Harder one. Bags on both pans this time. Five x plus two on the left, two x plus twenty on the right. Get the bags onto one side first.

ask.prompt: Take 2x from both sides of 5x + 2 = 2x + 20. What's left?

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Three x plus two equals twenty. Two bags off each pan, and it's still level.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Take two x off both pans. Five x take away two x is three x, and the right side loses its x. Three x plus two equals twenty.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: From there it's the same as before. Take two off both sides, and three x is eighteen. Divide by three, and x is six.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Check each side on its own. Left, thirty-two. Right, thirty-two. Level.

problem.setup: The line L has equation y = 3x − 4.

parts.text: The point (k, 11) lies on L. Find k.
Find the x-coordinate of the point where L crosses the x-axis.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Right, one set out like the exam papers now. Two parts, and the letter goes down before each one.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: The question gives us a line and calls it L. Its equation is y equals three x, minus four.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Part a. The point k, eleven sits on the line, so it fits the equation. Eleven goes in for y, and k for x.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Undo the minus four by adding four to both sides, which gives fifteen equals three k, and divide by three. k is five.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Part b. Where the line crosses the x-axis.

ask.prompt: Why is y = 0 where L crosses the x-axis?
choices: Every point on the x-axis has y = 0
x and y are equal there

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: That's it. On the x-axis you haven't gone up or down at all.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Every point on the x-axis is level with zero. Not up, not down. So y is zero there.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Add four, then divide by three. x is four over three. Leave it as a fraction. It's exact, and nobody asked you to round.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Check: three lots of four over three is four, take away four, zero.

sections.skipped: The map lists no second method for this idea; see notes.

sections.misconception: Multiplies only the first term in a bracket

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Found this under my bench. Somebody's working, and one of these lines isn't right. Have a look.

ask.prompt: Tap the line with the slip.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: That's the one. The four only got to the x. The minus two never got its share.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Look at the bracket. The four in front multiplies everything inside it. Did it?

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Here's how you'd catch it yourself. Put four back into the first line. The left side's four lots of two, which is eight, and the right side's fourteen. Not level.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So back on the bench. Four lots of x, and four lots of minus two: four x minus eight. That gives x equals seven, and seven checks out.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: I keep a tin of every bolt I've ever stripped. That slip's in there about six times.

intro.speaker: tin-can-tess
intro.say: Your go, and no help on the first try. Label the parts, and check each answer back in the equation.

fallback.setup: The line L has equation y = 2x + 5.

parts.text: The point (k, 17) lies on L. Find k.
Find the x-coordinate of the point where L crosses the x-axis.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Every part labelled, and every answer checked. That'd hold.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Heaps better than I did my first time.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Put your answer back into the equation. Does it come out level?

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: On the x-axis, y is zero. Start part b from there.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So. An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side, you do to the other. Undo the last thing first, then put your answer back in to check it's level.

board.write: 2. x terms on one side, numbers on the other

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Next time, two equations at once, with two unknowns. Two scales, one answer.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: The fella with the dog came back, by the way. Weighed the dog on its own this time.
